newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Hanbo probe has little impact on S.Korean stocks.
newsitem.headline: Hanbo probe has little impact on S.Korean stocks.

text.p: A televised briefing by state prosecutors on the Hanbo Steel loan scandal has had no impact on the Seoul stock market on Wednesday afternoon, brokers said.

Prosecutors said they had indicted 10 people in connection with the collapse of Hanbo Steel Co. Nine of those indicted, including three close aides to President Kim Young-sam, are already in custody. The tenth person to be charged is a former president of Korea First Bank.
The composite stock index rose 3.40 points to 710.34 in late afternoon.
"The outcome was widely expected. There were no surprises contained in the prosecutors' announcement," said Kim Duck-sun of Hyundai Securities.
Prosecutors said their probe into what is probably the biggest corporate collapse in South Korean history was now at the half-way stage.
Both Korea First Bank and Cho Hung Bank, both presidents of which were among those indicted, fell 30 won to 3,800 and 5,350 respectively.
